items.content_html:
The s3_service exposes it's respective client and bucket attributes publicly. I think this makes sense in the context of active storage, as it allows users to rely on the same adapter & configs that the framework is using for Activestorage without having to duplicate your own client and ensure it matches the original, which can be modified at runtime, in order to perform operations outside of the scope of ActiveStorage.

This commit serves to make the same true of the gcs_service, which currently defined it's respective client & bucket as private method definitions.

I did a bit of git snooping and didn't see any mention of this being an intentional decision when first released.

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
items.title: Refactor gcs_service public interface to bring more in line with s3_service

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #55845

Routes with optional segments currently treat nil values correctly (omitting them from the path), but empty strings ('') are not treated the same way. This creates malformed URLs with double slashes and incorrect query parameters.

This is particularly problematic because form parameters often come through as empty strings rather than nil, leading to inconsistent and unexpected behaviour.

Example:

# Route defined as:
get '(/a/:a_id)(/b/:b_id)(/c/:c_id)', to: 'test#index', as: :optional_segments

# With nil (works correctly):
optional_segments_path(a_id: nil, b_id: 2, c_id: 3)  # => "/b/2/c/3"

# With empty string (broken):
optional_segments_path(a_id: '', b_id: 2, c_id: 3)   # => "/a//b/2/c/3"

Detail

This PR normalizes blank values to nil for route parameters before path generation in ActionDispatch::Journey::Formatter#generate. The fix:

  1. Adds a small loop that checks each route parameter for blank values and converts them to nil
  2. Only affects actual route parameters (defined in the route pattern) - non-route parameters can still have blank values
  3. Leverages all existing nil-handling logic

The normalization happens before extract_parameterized_parts is called, which prevents blank route parameters from becoming query parameters like ?a_id=.

Additional information

Why normalize to nil instead of other approaches:

  • All existing logic already handles nil correctly (drop_while checks, compact!, query param filtering)
  • Minimal change - no modifications to existing logic needed
  • Preserves ability for non-route params to have blank values

items.content_html:
If you're using Active Storage, but don't have image_processing gem installed, because the [default analyzers]1 includes Vips and ImageMagick analyzers, you would see the following error:

[ActiveJob] Enqueued ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob ...
[ActiveJob] [ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob] Performing ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob ...
[ActiveJob] [ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob] [0efa0f81-23e0-4a09-9fb2-55ecb484c10a] Error performing ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob: NameError (uninitialized constant Vips):

Previously, this would rescue LoadError because the gems were required lazily.2

def read_image
  begin
    require "ruby-vips"
  rescue LoadError
    logger.info "Skipping image analysis because the ruby-vips gem isn't installed"
    return {}
  end

  # ...

Thanks to @claudiob for [reporting]3 and @Earlopain for all your help with this issue!

Footnotes

  1. https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#config-active-storage-analyzers ↩

  2. https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/ab8e833991e493f57f03c10ee2a8a7fda218faae/activestorage/lib/active_storage/analyzer/image_analyzer/vips.rb#L13-L18 ↩

  3. https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/55697#issuecomment-3364212327 ↩

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because we sometimes found ourselves manually preloading records because the standard preloading generated queries that were quite slow.
We found this was because the standard preloader tried to load associated records in a single query. While that is perfectly understandable, exactly the point of a preloader, but in some cases we want multiple queries that each retrieved a batch of the records to be preloaded.

Detail

This Pull Request adds an additional option to the preloader: batch_size. If that option is supplied the preloader limits the number of ids to be retrieved in a single query.

So when it has determined it needs to loads 10,000 categories, and batch size is set to 1,000, instead of doing a single query on the categories table supplying 10,000 ids it does 10 queries each retrieving 1,000 categories.

Especially when preloading belongs_to_and_has_many we found that the overall system performance was better splitting the preloader queries in multiple smaller ones.
items.title: Allow preloader queries to be split in batches

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Closes #55582.

Detail

When pluck, calculate, or ids are called on a relation with includes and limit/offset, they incorrectly apply the two-query eager loading strategy via distinct_relation_for_primary_key. This causes aggregation queries on empty tables to return [] instead of a row with null/zero values.

The two-query strategy exists to ensure the correct number of parent records are loaded when eager loading associations. For example, Post.eager_load(:comments).limit(5) should load exactly 5 posts, not 5 arbitrary join rows. However, pluck, calculate, and ids don't load records - they extract values. The optimization is unnecessary and breaks aggregation semantics.

This changes apply_join_dependency in these methods to pass eager_loading: false, skipping the two-query path. Aggregations now correctly return a result row even on empty relations, and limit applies to the result set rather than being used to select parent record IDs first. The pick method is also fixed since it calls pluck internally with a limit.

items.content_html:
Problem

The next release of basecamp/trix will support integrating with <form> element submissions without an associated <input type="hidden"> element (see basecamp/trix#1253 to learn more). The next release will also include support for <trix-editor> elements reading their initial value from their child content (see basecamp/trix#1128).

<trix-editor name="message[content]">
  <h1>hello world</h1>
</trix-editor>

Similarly, basecamp/lexxy (a potential Action Text-compatible successor to Trix) supports configuring its underlying editor with content captured through the block passed to its form helpers:

<%= form.rich_text_area :body do %>
  <lexxy-prompt trigger="@">
  </lexxy-prompt>
<% end %>

Its helper method monkey-patch already accepts and uses a block.

Proposal

This commit proposed that all Action Text-related form tag helpers accept &block arguments. In the short-term, there are no real changes to behavior: the captured content is treated the same way that a value argument or :value keyword argument would be. Trix will scrub and sanitize that content when its editor connects to the document.

In the long-term, this change will provide an additional integration and configuration opportunity for Action Text-compatible WYSIWYG text editors.

items.content_html:
Motivation and Background

Currently, when a validates_uniqueness_of validation fails, the errors.details hash only provides { error: :taken, ... }. This indicates that a conflict exists but offers no information about which record is causing the conflict.

This lack of context can be challenging in scenarios like building JSON APIs, where it would be highly beneficial to return a link or an ID to the conflicting resource.

This PR enhances the uniqueness validator to include the primary key of the conflicting record in the error details, providing developers with more actionable information.

This change was proposed and received positive feedback in the following Rails Discuss thread:
https://discuss.rubyonrails.org/t/proposal-include-existing-record-id-in-uniqueness-validation-error-details/89810

Implementation

The core of this change is in ActiveRecord::Validations::UniquenessValidator. The existing database check, which used .exists?, has been replaced with a call to .pick(klass.primary_key).

If a conflicting record is found, its ID is now added to the errors.details hash under the new key :existing_id.

Before this change:

topic.errors.details[:title]
# => [{error: :taken, value: "Existing Topic"}]

After this change:

topic.errors.details[:title]
# => [{error: :taken, value: "Existing Topic", existing_id: 1}]

This change applies to both simple and scoped uniqueness validations.

Click to see the benchmark script used 
#!/usr/bin/env ruby

# Benchmark script for uniqueness validation existing_id feature
# Based on Rails contributing guide: [https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#benchmark-your-code](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#benchmark-your-code)

require "bundler/setup"
require "benchmark/ips"
require "active_record"
require "sqlite3"

# Setup in-memory database
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")

# Create test table and model
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute <<-SQL
  CREATE TABLE benchmark_topics (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    author_name VARCHAR(255)
  )
SQL

class BenchmarkTopic < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.table_name = "benchmark_topics"
  validates_uniqueness_of :title
  validates_uniqueness_of :author_name, scope: :title
end

# Create test data
puts "Setting up test data..."
existing_topic = BenchmarkTopic.create!(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "John Doe")
BenchmarkTopic.create!(title: "Another Topic", author_name: "Jane Smith")

# Create new instances that will fail validation (to trigger the existing_id logic)
BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "Different Author")
BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "John Doe")

puts "\n=== Benchmarking Uniqueness Validation Performance ==="
puts "Commit: #{`git rev-parse --short HEAD`.strip} - #{`git log --oneline -1 --pretty=format:'%s'`.strip}"
puts "Ruby: #{RUBY_VERSION}"
puts "ActiveRecord: #{ActiveRecord::VERSION::STRING}"
puts

Benchmark.ips do |x|
  x.config(time: 5, warmup: 2)

  x.report("simple uniqueness validation (with existing_id)") do
    topic = BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "Different Author")
    topic.valid?
  end

  x.report("scoped uniqueness validation (with existing_id)") do
    topic = BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "John Doe")
    topic.valid?
  end

  x.report("successful validation (no existing_id logic)") do
    topic = BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Unique Title #{rand(10000)}", author_name: "Unique Author")
    topic.valid?
  end

  x.compare!
end

puts "\n=== Memory and Error Details Analysis ==="

# Test memory usage and error details
require "objspace"

before_count = ObjectSpace.count_objects[:T_OBJECT]

# Trigger validation errors to test existing_id functionality
100.times do |i|
  topic = BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "Author #{i}")
  topic.valid?
end

after_count = ObjectSpace.count_objects[:T_OBJECT]

puts "Object creation during 100 validations: #{after_count - before_count} objects"

# Verify the existing_id functionality
puts "\n=== Existing ID Functionality Verification ==="
test_topic = BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "Test Author")
test_topic.valid?

error_details = test_topic.errors.details[:title]
puts "Error details: #{error_details}"

if error_details.any? && error_details.first[:existing_id]
  puts "✓ existing_id feature working: #{error_details.first[:existing_id]}"
  puts "✓ Matches existing topic ID: #{existing_topic.id}"
else
  puts "✗ existing_id feature not found in error details"
end

# Test scoped validation
scoped_topic = BenchmarkTopic.new(title: "Existing Topic", author_name: "John Doe")
scoped_topic.valid?

scoped_error_details = scoped_topic.errors.details[:author_name]
puts "Scoped error details: #{scoped_error_details}"

if scoped_error_details.any? && scoped_error_details.first[:existing_id]
  puts "✓ Scoped existing_id feature working: #{scoped_error_details.first[:existing_id]}"
else
  puts "✗ Scoped existing_id feature not found in error details"
end

puts "\n=== Performance Comparison Analysis ==="
puts "This benchmark measures:"
puts "1. Simple uniqueness validation performance with existing_id lookup"
puts "2. Scoped uniqueness validation performance with existing_id lookup"
puts "3. Successful validation performance (baseline - no existing_id lookup needed)"
puts
puts "The existing_id feature adds a database query (.pick(primary_key)) instead of .exists?"
puts "This provides the ID of the conflicting record but may have slight performance impact."

items.content_html:
Related to #26547, fixes #25333. Follow-up/related to #55824.

Motivation / Background

When subscribing to Action Cable Streams during Channel subscription, Action Cable defers transmitting the subscription confirmation until the Streams are subscribed. This meant that after_subscribe callbacks would be called before the Channel Subscription confirmation is transmitted. This PR defers the after_subscribe callback until after the subscription confirmation is transmitted.

⚠️ This does change the authorization lifecycle. Previously it was possible to reject a subscription in the after_subscribe callback because that callback was always invoked before the channel subscription confirmation was transmitted.

rails/actioncable/lib/action_cable/channel/base.rb

Lines 194 to 201 in dac26fd

def subscribe_to_channel
run_callbacks :subscribe do
subscribed
end
reject_subscription if subscription_rejected?
ensure_confirmation_sent
end

That seems unintentional because the callback docs imply rejection should happen before:

# This callback will be triggered after the Base#subscribed method is called,
# even if the subscription was rejected with the Base#reject method.
#
# To trigger the callback only on successful subscriptions, use the
# Base#subscription_rejected? method:
#
#     after_subscribe :my_method, unless: :subscription_rejected?
#
def after_subscribe(*methods, &block)

I didn't find any visible source evidence of reject being used in an after_subscribe, but it's possible.

If that seems like a dealbreaker, we can introduce a new callback (after_confirm) to perform this role instead.
